summary: Re-tested the iteration_7 fixes. The HIGH preview token expiry bug is fixed. GET /api/videos/{id}/play-url returns a signed /file URL (uid, exp, sig) that lasts 6h. In Library, the preview <video> src now uses sig= instead of auth=. In the browser: uploaded a 200s VP9 WebM, opened the preview, paused, waited 80s, then seeked to 170s. The Range requests returned 206 (bytes=10223616-, bytes=8519680-), playback resumed at 174s and no 401 occurred. Backend: 46/46 pytest pass (the 40 old tests plus 6 new ones in test_play_url.py). The long upload script works: 183 MB, 360s 1280x720 -> long; 20s 720x1280 -> short.

minor.issue: Content-Length now equals size (verified 2826209 matches the file). It still returns 200 without Accept-Ranges and ignores the Range header, so seeking doesn't work for the first preview after cache eviction until the background rebuild finishes. Known since iteration_7; low impact.

action_items: Optional MINOR: in the /file parts-stream path, honour Range (or wait briefly for the cache) and send Accept-Ranges.
critical_code_review_comments: The signed URL is a bearer link: anyone who has it can fetch the video for 6h. That's acceptable for previews, but don't log full URLs. Deleting the video revokes access because /file checks is_deleted.

_media_sig signs 'vid:uid:exp' joined with ':'. Collisions are theoretically possible if ids contain ':'. Here they can't, because the ownership check requires the video to belong to that uid. Low risk.
The HMAC key is derived from CLERK_SECRET_KEY, so rotating the Clerk key invalidates all play URLs. That's fine, but a dedicated MEDIA_SIGNING_KEY would separate the two concerns.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (preview via play-url, seek after 80s OK, upload, delete)
